newsitem.title: TURKEY: Istanbul gold prices edge higher in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Istanbul gold prices edge higher in thin trade.

text.p: Prices firmed slightly on the Istanbul Gold Exchange in weak trade on Wednesday due to low demand and uncertainty over world values.
Gold closed at $383.00 an ounce, up from $382.50 on Tuesday and 1,213,600 lira per gram after 1,208,300. Volume tumbled from Tuesday's 1,031 kilos to 483 kilos.

"Players were unwilling to take new positions amid expectations that ounce prices faced resistance in world markets. Public demand is naturally very thin after the ending of the summer season," said one bank dealer.
The increase in gold's lira price was largely due to the lira's continued weakness against the dollar. The lira closed at 98,410 per dollar versus Tuesday's 97,960.
The morning session saw 403 kilos traded, followed by only 80 kilos in the afternoon. 55.5 percent of the total trade was conducted in lira terms. --Istanbul newsroom +90-212-2750875
